title: diagnostic-oom-driver-hypotheses-scratch
content:
Quick scratchpad — do not treat as final. Goal: capture commands, error snippets, timelines, and hypotheses for recurring OOM-like crashes on k8s nodes (p5/gp102) when running batched inference with kv-cache warming. Context: intermittent crashes over last 2 weeks, suspects: driver/libcuda ABI drift, mixed libcuda/libnvidia-open, and kernel upgrade timing.

Summary of observed symptoms:
- Process exits with CUDA OOM (RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory) but NVML reports free memory > model allocation immediately after crash.
- dmesg shows 'oom-killer' touching unrelated process or no oom-killer entry depending on node.
- Container logs include: "failed to allocate 2147483648 bytes on device 0: CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY" followed by rapid restart loop.
- Sometimes we also see: "undefined symbol: cuInit" or ld.so complaining about libcuda.so.1: wrong ELF class or version mismatch.
- Reproduced locally once on node with mixed driver packages (nvidia-driver-535 + libcuda from 540 staging) — reproducible with simple memtest script below.

Commands I ran and outputs (trimmed):
1) nvidia-smi -a
Timestamp                       : Mon Feb 28 12:17:03 2026
Driver Version                  : 535.98
CUDA Version                    : 12.2
Attached GPUs                   : 1
FB Memory Usage                 : 12012MiB / 24268MiB
Processes: ID, Type, GPU Memory
  2345      C+G    11000MiB  (inference process)

2) python -c 'import torch; print(torch.version.cuda); print(torch.cuda.get_device_properties(0))'
'11.8'  <-- mismatch: runtime reports torch built against CUDA 11.8 but system CUDA is 12.2

3) ls -l /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so*
lrwxrwxrwx 1 root root 14 Jan 15  /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so -> libcuda.so.1
-rw-r--r-- 1 root root  6.2M Jan 15 /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1  <-- file present (from driver 535 package)

4) readelf -sW /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1 | grep cuInit
  102: 000000000002f8b0   34 FUNC    GLOBAL DEFAULT   16 cuInit@GLIBC_PRIVATE

5) Docker container logs snippet:
RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 2.00 GiB (GPU 0; 24.00 GiB total capacity; 20.90 GiB already allocated; 3.10 GiB free)
During handling of the above exception, another exception occurred:
OSError: libcudart.so.11.0: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory

Interpretation: mixed signs — PyTorch complaining about memory, then post-failure the runtime tries to call into a different CUDA runtime library and fails to load it. Suggests that at crash time the process may be in an inconsistent state where some addresses are mapped to different GLIBC_PRIVATE sym versions.

Minimal repro (local) - mem_hammer.py:
# allocate large tensors in loop and touch kv cache sim
import torch, time
for i in range(200):
    a = torch.empty((1024,1024,32), dtype=torch.float16, device='cuda')
    a.normal_()
    time.sleep(0.05)
    if i % 10 == 0:
        torch.cuda.empty_cache()

On a node with driver+lib mismatch this leads to: kernel panic in nvidia_uvm or silent process exit.

Other logs of interest:
- dmesg tail after one crash: 
[Feb28 12:18:07] NVRM: GPU at 0000:03:00.0: RmInitAdapter failed! (error=3)
[Feb28 12:18:07] NVRM: GPU 0000:03:00.0: GPU is lost
[Feb28 12:18:07] kernel: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:03:00): 13, pid=2345, GPU has fallen off the bus

- journalctl for container runtime: 
Mar 01 03:34:01 node-17 dockerd[2890]: time="2026-03-01T03:34:01Z" level=error msg="failed to start container: driver failed programming external connectivity on endpoint..."

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Library/driver ABI mismatch: userspace sees libcuda.so from one driver version but kernel module/version expects another -> NVML reports inconsistent state, some functions missing (cuInit symbol issues). Explains 'cuInit' and libcuda version errors.
2) UVM kernel module crashes under specific allocation patterns (large contiguous pinned pages), causing the kernel to mark GPU lost and subsequent user processes get weird OOM or symbol errors when runtime tries to reinit.
3) Namespace/sandboxing mismatch: container image vendors different glibc/CUDA runtime (conda + cudatoolkit) vs host drivers -> at process restart time loader picks host libs or container overlay libs unpredictably.
4) Race between driver update and container restarts: nodes that had driver package upgraded but not rebooted show intermittent behavior.

What I tried (and results):
- Reinstalling driver 535 on affected node -> briefly stable, then reproduction within hours when we run larger batch sizes.
- Pinning torch to cuda11.8 build version in container image -> reduced frequency but did not eliminate (suggests partial mitigation).
- Forced module reload (modprobe -r nvidia_uvm; modprobe nvidia_uvm) -> when successful, GPU comes back; if module unload fails, node needs reboot.
- Running small reproducer under nsjail / pivot_root -> same fail mode, so not purely k8s kubelet/CRI-specific.

Immediate next steps (practical):
- Add a short e2e job that repeatedly runs mem_hammer.py on a staging p5 fleet with driver version matrix (532, 535, 540) to capture kernel logs and nvdec dumps. Capture kdump if available.
- Add LD_DEBUG=libs and ldd python binary output to our crash wrapper to capture which libcuda/libcudart are being resolved at launch vs at crash time.
- Create a short kube daemonset that periodically attempts modprobe -r nvidia_uvm and logs success/failure: this will tell us if module unload races exist.
- Open a tracking ticket (JIRA-ENG-4123) with kernel dmesg, NVML traces, and representative container images.

Longer-term ideas:
- Harden container runtime: pre-load and RTLD_DEEPBIND libcuda from host during startup so userland cannot mask it with conda's cudatoolkit. Test for regressions.
- Work with driver vendor to get a backtrace from uvm when crash occurs (requires repro and kdump).

Notes to self:
- When reproducing locally, capture everything: /var/log/kern.log, sudo dmesg -T >dmesg.txt, nvidia-smi -q -x >nvidia-smi.xml, and strace -f -s 200 -o strace.out on the python launcher to see loader activity.
- If you see 'GPU has fallen off the bus' Xid 13 consistently, prioritize module/kern side fix over torch-level workarounds.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Is there any node pool that was updated without reboot in the last 30 days? (ask infra infra-updates channel)
- Can we get kernel oops logs shipped automatically to our centralized logging when node reboots? (SRE task)
- Are other teams (Vision team) seeing similar silent exits? Jared to check.

TODO:
- [ ] Add repro job to CI matrix (staging only) - blocked by infra quota request
- [ ] Collect driver package manifests from all failing nodes
- [ ] Run ldconfig snapshots before/after container start on failing nodes
- [ ] Draft Slack thread summary for ENG and SRE channels with repro steps (include mem_hammer.py)

If I come back to this in >1 week: start by rerunning mem_hammer with env vars: CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1, LD_PRELOAD=/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1, LD_DEBUG=libs.

-- end of scratchpad --
